project.title: SGEMM GPU Kernel Performance - Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
project.description: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) implementation from scratch (Random With Replacement vs. Random Without Replacement) on the SGEMM GPU Kernel Performance dataset across various batch sizes.
project.author: Santanu Samanta

dataset.name: SGEMM GPU Kernel Performance Dataset
dataset.target: Log-transformed and averaged execution time (Run1 to Run4 in ms)

strategies.name: Random With Replacement
strategies.description: Batches are sampled randomly with replacement during each epoch iteration.

strategies.name: Random Without Replacement
strategies.description: Data indices are shuffled randomly at the start of each epoch and traversed sequentially without replacement.

gfg_breakdown_sections.title: 1. Loss Function: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
gfg_breakdown_sections.intuition: To measure how well our linear model predicts GPU kernel runtime execution, we calculate the Average Mean Squared Error. Including the scaling factor 1/(2n) elegantly simplifies the derivative calculation during backpropagation.

gfg_breakdown_sections.title: 2. Gradient Derivation (Weights & Bias)
gfg_breakdown_sections.intuition: Using chain rule calculus, we compute partial derivatives of the Mean Squared Error loss with respect to weight vector W and scalar bias. This determines the steepest direction of error increase, which we subtract during parameter updates.

gfg_breakdown_sections.title: 3. SGD Strategy 1: Random With Replacement
gfg_breakdown_sections.intuition: In Random With Replacement, sample indices are drawn uniformly at random with replacement using np.random.choice(). This models a true probabilistic sampling process where individual instances can appear multiple times per epoch.
gfg_breakdown_sections.formula: Index k ~ Uniform(1, m) with replacement for k in [1, ceiling(m / batch_size)]
gfg_breakdown_sections.code_snippet:
def sgd_RWR(X, Y, alpha=0.01, epochs=100, batch_size=240, bias=0):
    m, n = X.shape
    w = np.zeros(n)
    itt_per_epoch = int(np.ceil(m / batch_size))
    loss_plot = []
    for i in range(epochs):
        for j in range(itt_per_epoch):
            indexes = np.random.choice(m, size=batch_size, replace=True)
            X_batch, Y_batch = X[indexes], Y[indexes]
            w -= alpha * gradw(X_batch, Y_batch, w, bias)
            bias -= alpha * gradb(X_batch, Y_batch, w, bias)
        loss_plot.append(MSE(X, Y, w, bias))
    return w, bias, loss_plot

gfg_breakdown_sections.title: 4. SGD Strategy 2: Random Without Replacement
gfg_breakdown_sections.intuition: Random Without Replacement shuffles the dataset indices once at the beginning of every epoch using np.random.permutation(). Traversing sequential chunks guarantees every sample is visited exactly once per epoch, lowering variance.
gfg_breakdown_sections.formula: Permutation π = Shuffle([1, ..., m]), Batch j = X[j : j + batch_size]
gfg_breakdown_sections.code_snippet:
def sgd_RWOR(X, Y, alpha=0.01, epochs=100, batch_size=240, bias=0):
    m, n = X.shape
    w = np.zeros(n)
    loss_plot = []
    for i in range(epochs):
        indexes = np.random.permutation(m)
        X_perm, Y_perm = X[indexes], Y[indexes]
        for j in range(0, m, batch_size):
            X_batch = X_perm[j:j+batch_size]
            Y_batch = Y_perm[j:j+batch_size]
            w -= alpha * gradw(X_batch, Y_batch, w, bias)
            bias -= alpha * gradb(X_batch, Y_batch, w, bias)
        loss_plot.append(MSE(X, Y, w, bias))
    return w, bias, loss_plot
